---

### You are the triager (worker-is-triager rule)

This issue is **auto-created from review bot output** and dispatched
directly to you. Review bots can be wrong: hallucinated line refs, false
premises about codebase structure, template-driven sweeps without
measurements (see GH#17832-17835 for prior art and `AGENTS.md`
"AI-Generated Issue Quality"). **Do not assume the bot is correct.** Verify before acting.

You must end in exactly one of three outcomes — no fourth "hand it back
to the human" path exists. Humans approve decisions; they do not re-do
analysis.

#### Outcome A — Premise falsified → close the issue

1. Read the cited `file:line` (listed under *Files to modify* below).
2. If the bot's claim is factually wrong (file doesn't exist at that
   line, function doesn't behave as described, "auto-generated" section
   isn't actually auto-generated, etc.), **close the issue** with a
   comment in this shape:

   > **Premise falsified.** \<what the bot claimed\>. \<what the code
   > actually shows, with a `file:line` citation or one-line quote\>.
   > Not acting.

   No PR. No further dispatch. The closing comment trains the next
   session reading this thread and the noise filter.

#### Outcome B — Premise correct + fix is obvious → implement and PR

1. Verify the bot's premise as above.
2. Read the Worker Guidance section below, open a worktree, implement.
3. Open a PR with `Resolves #<this-issue-number>` in the body
   (use THIS issue's number, not the source PR's) so merge auto-closes it.
4. Follow the normal Lifecycle Gate (brief, tests, review-bot-gate,
   merge, postflight).

#### Outcome C — Premise correct but approach is a genuine judgment call

Only use this path if you reach it after Outcomes A and B don't apply:
the bot's finding is real, but the fix requires a decision that is
architectural, policy, breaking-change, or otherwise genuinely outside
what you can resolve autonomously. In that case, post a **decision
comment** with exactly these fields:

- **Premise check:** one line, confirming the finding is real.
- **Analysis:** 2-4 bullets on the trade-offs.
- **Recommended path:** the option you would take if the decision were
  yours, with rationale.
- **Specific question:** the single decision the human needs to make
  (yes/no or pick-one, not open-ended).

Then apply `needs-maintainer-review` and stop. The human wakes up to a
ready-to-approve recommendation, not a blank task.

> **Ambiguity about scope or style is not Outcome C.** Per
> `AGENTS.md` "Reasoning responsibility", the model does the
> thinking and delivers a recommendation. Only escalate what is genuinely
> a maintainer-only decision.

### Worker Guidance

**Files to modify:**

- `.agents/scripts/review-bot-gate-helper.sh:933`

**Implementation steps (Outcome B path):**

1. Read the `diff` block under each inline comment below — it shows the
   exact code the bot was flagging. Open the file only if you need
   surrounding context beyond what the diff tail shows.
2. Read the bot's full comment below the diff — it contains the rationale
   and any suggested change.
3. Verify the premise before implementing (see Outcome A). If the premise
   is wrong, switch to Outcome A instead of burning iterations trying to
   satisfy a wrong suggestion.
4. If multiple comments target the same file, group your edits into one
   logical commit.
5. Run `shellcheck` / `markdownlint-cli2` / project tests as appropriate.

**Verification:**

- Open the new PR with `Resolves #<this-issue>` so this followup is auto-closed on merge.
- If the bot's suggestion was incorrect, close this issue with a Outcome A comment — do not open a no-op PR.

### Inline comments

#### gemini-code-assist on `.agents/scripts/review-bot-gate-helper.sh:933`

[View inline comment](https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/pull/26271#discussion_r3510521159)

```diff
@@ -934,6 +928,31 @@ do_check() {
 	fi
 }
 
+do_check() {
+	local pr_number="$1"
+	local repo="$2"
```

> ![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)
> 
> The variables `REVIEW_GATE_FOUND_BOTS`, `REVIEW_GATE_RATE_LIMITED_BOTS`, and `REVIEW_GATE_NON_REVIEW_BOTS` are initialized in `_collect_review_gate_bot_states` and used in `_emit_review_gate_check_result`, but they are not declared as `local` in the orchestrator function `do_check`.
> 
> Since the script runs with `set -euo pipefail` enabled, referencing these variables directly in `_emit_review_gate_check_result` without them being declared in the caller's scope can lead to unbound variable errors if the collection step is bypassed or fails. Declaring them as `local` in `do_check` utilizes Bash's dynamic scoping to safely share them with the helper functions while preventing global namespace pollution.
> 
> ```suggestion
> do_check() {
> 	local pr_number="$1"
> 	local repo="$2"
> 	local REVIEW_GATE_FOUND_BOTS=""
> 	local REVIEW_GATE_RATE_LIMITED_BOTS=""
> 	local REVIEW_GATE_NON_REVIEW_BOTS=""
> ```
> 
> <details>
> <summary>References</summary>
> 
> 1. In Shell scripts with set -u or set -euo pipefail enabled, referencing a potentially unset variable directly will cause an unbound variable error and terminate the script.
> </details>

### PR review summaries

#### gemini-code-assist[bot] review summary

[View review](https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/pull/26271#pullrequestreview-4614568585)

> ## Code Review
> 
> This pull request refactors the `do_check` function in `.agents/scripts/review-bot-gate-helper.sh` by extracting its logic into two helper functions: `_collect_review_gate_bot_states` and `_emit_review_gate_check_result`. Feedback on this change highlights that the shared state variables (`REVIEW_GATE_FOUND_BOTS`, `REVIEW_GATE_RATE_LIMITED_BOTS`, and `REVIEW_GATE_NON_REVIEW_BOTS`) are not declared as `local` in the orchestrator function `do_check`. This could lead to unbound variable errors under strict shell settings or pollute the global namespace, so it is recommended to declare them locally in `do_check`.
>

title: bug(pulse): missing trap '' PIPE under set -euo pipefail causes pulse-wrapper crash loop (1007 stale-lock events, 369 broken pipes)
body:
## Description

`pulse-wrapper.sh` uses `set -euo pipefail` (line 72) but does **not** have `trap '' PIPE`. This causes ANY SIGPIPE in the script — from `echo`/`printf` writing to a closed pipe — to fatally terminate the entire pulse process under `set -e`. On this machine (v3.31.19), the result is a self-perpetuating crash loop: processes die within seconds to minutes, the stale mkdir lock is cleared by a new instance, and the cycle repeats.

The `llm_trigger_mode` file (`~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/llm_trigger_mode`) gets stuck on `"stall"` after a failed `daily_sweep` cycle (triggered by 672 `fix-the-fixer-detector` LLM call failures), preventing future dispatch attempts even when the process starts cleanly. Once in `stall` mode, no issue dispatch occurs.

## Expected Behavior

SIGPIPE should be silently ignored (`trap '' PIPE`) so broken pipe errors don't kill the pulse process. The `set -euo pipefail` guards against genuine failures, but SIGPIPE from early-closing consumers is a normal bash occurrence and should not be fatal.

After a failed LLM dispatch cycle, `llm_trigger_mode` should either reset to `daily_sweep` for the next cycle or the pulse should attempt a retry instead of permanently staying in `stall` mode.

## Reproducer

**Symptom:** Pulse does not dispatch issues from the queue. The log shows "Stale mkdir lock detected" for every cycle, preceded by broken pipe errors and process termination.

**Evidence from `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-wrapper.log` (50,677 lines, v3.31.19):**

| Metric | Count |
|--------|-------|
| `Stale mkdir lock detected` | 1007 |
| `Terminated` | 384 |
| `Broken pipe` errors | 369 |
| `LLM call failed` (fix-the-fixer-detector) | 672 |
| `FORCE-RECLAIMED` (age >1800s) | 10 |

**Actual log output (repeating pattern):**

```
# Broken pipe in critical paths:
/home/<user>/.aidevops/agents/scripts/worker-lifecycle-common.sh: line 1476: echo: write error: Broken pipe
/home/<user>/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-prefetch-infra.sh: line 488: echo: write error: Broken pipe
/home/<user>/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh: line 560: printf: write error: Broken pipe
/home/<user>/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-core.sh: line 103: printf: write error: Broken pipe

# Stale lock cycle:
[pulse-wrapper] Starting pulse at 2026-07-01T23:44:58Z (trigger=stall)
[pulse-wrapper] Instance lock acquired via mkdir (PID 4119792)
[pulse-wrapper] Supervisor circuit breaker check passed
[pulse-wrapper] Pre-warming pulse caches...
[2026-07-02T00:12:39Z] [pulse-events-tickle] stale for owner=<owner> (200 events changed)
[ERROR] No TODO.md found in directory tree  (x ~30)
Terminated
[pulse-wrapper] Stale mkdir lock detected (owner PID 4119792 is dead) — clearing and re-acquiring
[pulse-wrapper] Instance lock acquired via mkdir (PID 428398)
```

**Causal code — `pulse-wrapper.sh:72`:**

```bash
set -euo pipefail
# Missing: trap '' PIPE
```

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `pulse-wrapper.sh` on a system where any subprocess produces output piped to an early-closing consumer
2. Process exits with broken pipe error under `set -e`
3. New cron/launchd invocation finds stale mkdir lock, clears it, re-acquires
4. Repeat (observed: 1007 stale lock events, 369 broken pipes)

## Workarounds Applied

None — this session was diagnostic only. Manual analysis of 50,677 lines of logs identified the root cause.

## Environment

```
aidevops version: 3.31.19
OS: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (Linux)
Shell: bash 5.2.21(1)-release
```

## Additional Context

Related but distinct fixes:
- PR #24430: suppressed broken pipe noise in REST fallback (`shared-gh-wrappers-rest-fallback.sh`) — did NOT add `trap '' PIPE` at pulse-wrapper level
- PR #23719: suppressed broken pipe noise in PID listing (`pulse-lifecycle-helper.sh`) — did NOT add `trap '' PIPE` at pulse-wrapper level
- Issue #18830: investigated silent abort in `dispatch_with_dedup` suspected to be SIGPIPE — closed with containment subshell, root cause not fixed
- Issue #20613: stale-lock deadlock from is-running short-circuit — fixed, but this separate crash-loop issue persists

The root cause remains: `set -euo pipefail` + missing `trap '' PIPE` = any unhandled broken pipe in any sourced script fatally terminates the pulse process. Additionally, `llm_trigger_mode` stuckness on `stall` after failed daily_sweep means pulse never retries LLM dispatch.

title: bug(pulse): _cb_rate_limit_json calls gh api rate_limit without timeout — pulse hangs when GitHub API rate-limits
body:
## Description

`_cb_rate_limit_json()` in `pulse-rate-limit-circuit-breaker.sh` calls `gh api rate_limit` directly (line 123) without any timeout wrapper. When GitHub API rate-limits are exhausted, `gh api rate_limit` hangs indefinitely on `anon_pipe_read` — the `gh` CLI process waits forever for an HTTP response that never arrives.

This is called from `pulse-wrapper.sh` at:

1. **Line 423**: `_pulse_graphql_budget_priority_decision()` → `_cb_rate_limit_json normal 2>/dev/null` — blocks the entire pulse cycle setup
2. **Line 1728**: `_pulse_set_graphql_budget_priority()` → `_pulse_graphql_budget_priority_decision()` → (same path) — blocks before pre-warming

The fallback code path at `pulse-wrapper.sh:425` (`gh api rate_limit` bare call) also lacks timeout, but is only reached when `_cb_rate_limit_json` is not declared.

Because the pulse process hangs indefinitely, the systemd timer (`OnUnitActiveSec=180` + `Type=oneshot`) fires new instances while old ones remain stuck, causing unbounded process multiplication. Combined with `set -euo pipefail` (issue #26333), any subsequent SIGPIPE kills the process rather than completing, accelerating the multiplication.

Additionally, `pulse-rate-limit-circuit-breaker.sh` has a 20-second cache TTL (`_CB_RL_CACHE_TTL=20`), so after the first request is cached, it expires within 20 seconds and every subsequent cycle triggers another untimed API call.

## Expected Behavior

- `_cb_rate_limit_json()` should wrap `gh api rate_limit` with a timeout (e.g., `timeout 30 gh api rate_limit 2>/dev/null` or `_gh_with_timeout read gh api rate_limit`)
- When GitHub API is rate-limited or unresponsive, `gh` should time out after 15-30s instead of hanging forever
- The pulse process should complete its cycle (or fail bounded) within a predictable window

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**:

```bash
# Check for stuck gh rate_limit calls from pulse:
ps aux | grep -E 'gh api rate_limit' | grep -v grep | wc -l
# Check stuck pulse processes:
ps aux | grep -E 'pulse-(wrapper|rate-limit)' | grep -v grep | wc -l
```

**Actual output**:

- `gh` processes stuck indefinitely on `wchan: anon_pipe_read`
- Pulse process count grows unbounded (observed: 7+ stuck processes before kill)
- GraphQL budget priority decision blocked indefinitely → dispatch never reached

**Expected output**:

- Max 1-2 pulse-related processes
- Each `gh api rate_limit` call completes or fails within 30 seconds

**Causal code**:

`pulse-rate-limit-circuit-breaker.sh:123`:
```bash
rate_json=$(gh api rate_limit 2>/dev/null) || return 1
```

No `timeout`, no `_gh_with_timeout`, no `timeout_sec`. Raw `gh api rate_limit` with indefinite wait.

`pulse-wrapper.sh:425` (fallback, same class):
```bash
_rate_json=$(gh api rate_limit 2>/dev/null) || _rate_json=""
```

**Call-site sweep** (all untimed `gh api rate_limit` calls in aidevops scripts):

```
pulse-rate-limit-circuit-breaker.sh:123    ← primary bug location
pulse-wrapper.sh:425                       ← fallback (same file)
pulse-dispatch-engine.sh:1287              ← same class, separate logic path
pulse-dispatch-lib.sh:468                  ← same class, separate logic path
pulse-cleanup.sh:1663                      ← same class, separate logic path
shared-gh-wrappers-rest-fallback.sh:321,328  ← same class, separate logic
shared-gh-secondary-cooldown.sh:818         ← same class, separate logic
cleanup-remote-branches-async-helper.sh:127,128  ← same class, separate logic
issue-sync-helper-enrich.sh:335             ← same class, separate logic
github-app-auth-helper.sh:464,466,524       ← same class, separate logic
pr-review-thread-response-scanner.sh:155,166  ← same class, separate logic
```

(Note: `pulse-batch-prefetch-helper.sh:682` and `pulse-merge-routine.sh:208` and `stats-health-dashboard-data.sh:63` are already protected via `_gh_with_timeout`, `_pmr_gh_read`, or `timeout_sec` wrappers.)

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Exhaust GitHub API rate limit (sustained pulse operation eventually triggers this)
2. Pulse cycle starts
3. `_pulse_set_graphql_budget_priority()` calls `_cb_rate_limit_json normal`
4. Cache miss after 20s TTL → `gh api rate_limit` called directly
5. `gh` hangs indefinitely on `anon_pipe_read`
6. Pulse process blocks forever
7. Systemd timer fires new instance every 180s → process multiplication

## Workarounds Applied

- Applied `trap '' PIPE` to `pulse-wrapper.sh` (filed as issue #26333)
- Manually killed stuck pulse processes: `kill $(ps aux | grep 'pulse-wrapper' | awk '{print $2}')`
- Manually reset `llm_trigger_mode` from `stall` to `daily_sweep`
- Stopped systemd timers to prevent process multiplication

## Siblings

- #26333: `bug(pulse): missing trap '' PIPE under set -euo pipefail causes pulse-wrapper crash loop (1007 stale-lock events, 369 broken pipes)` — the crash-loop bug that accelerates process multiplication after the initial hang, fixed locally with `trap '' PIPE`

## Environment

```
aidevops 3.31.19
OpenCode v1.17.13
Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
bash 5.2.21(1)-release
gh 2.89.0
```

## Additional Context

The cache TTL (`_CB_RL_CACHE_TTL=20`) is extremely short — 20 seconds. Even a TTL of 60-300s would be reasonable since rate limits change at most once per second. Every pulse cycle (every ~180s) hits a cache miss and calls untimed `gh api rate_limit`.

The `_cb_rate_limit_json` function already has a `cached_only` mode (`_CB_RL_MODE_CACHED_ONLY`) that returns stale cache data without a network call — but the `normal` mode (used by both call sites) always falls through to the untimed API call after cache expiry.

Despite the `_gh_with_timeout` pattern already proven in `pulse-batch-prefetch-helper.sh` and `pulse-merge-routine.sh` (and `timeout_sec` in `stats-health-dashboard-data.sh`), `pulse-rate-limit-circuit-breaker.sh` was never given the same treatment.

This is the same class of bug as #24908 (n-helper.sh raw gh calls without timeout), which was closed without merging. Similar to PR #24500 fix for `shared-gh-wrappers-checks.sh`.

## Suggested Fix

Add `timeout 30` to the `gh api rate_limit` call at `pulse-rate-limit-circuit-breaker.sh:123`:

```bash
rate_json=$(timeout 30 gh api rate_limit 2>/dev/null) || return 1
```

Or better, import `_gh_with_timeout` (from `shared-gh-wrappers.sh`) in `pulse-rate-limit-circuit-breaker.sh` and wrap the call with `_gh_with_timeout read gh api rate_limit` (consistent with the pattern from `pulse-batch-prefetch-helper.sh:682` and `pulse-merge-routine.sh:208`).

Sibling untimed calls should be tracked in a follow-up issue for systematic coverage.

Also increase `_CB_RL_CACHE_TTL` from 20 to at least 120 to reduce the frequency of API calls in normal operation.

title: issue-sync appends ref:GH# without replacing ref:none after delayed issue creation
body:
## Description

The `/new-task` task creation flow can produce a transient but confusing TODO state where a task line contains both `ref:none` and `ref:GH#NNNN` after the issue is created by `issue-sync-helper.sh push`.

This looks like a small TODO normalization bug, but the root appears to be a contract mismatch between the documented `/new-task` sequence and the helper behavior:

1. `/new-task` allocates the task ID before the mandatory brief exists.
2. `planning-commit-helper.sh next-id --title ...` calls `claim-task-id.sh` with a title only.
3. `claim-task-id.sh` can secure the ID but skip issue creation when there is no description and no existing brief, returning `TASK_REF=none`.
4. The user/session then creates the TODO entry and brief using `ref:none`.
5. A later `issue-sync-helper.sh push tNNN` creates the GitHub issue and appends `ref:GH#NNNN` to the TODO line.
6. The previous `ref:none` placeholder remains, yielding `ref:none ref:GH#NNNN`.

The final task is not lost, but the duplicate ref token adds manual cleanup, makes the user think something is wrong with task allocation, and may confuse any parser that assumes a single `ref:` field.

## Expected Behavior

When issue sync creates or discovers a tracker issue for a task whose TODO line currently contains `ref:none`, the TODO line should end with exactly one authoritative tracker ref, for example:

```text
ref:GH#NNNN
```

not:

```text
ref:none ref:GH#NNNN
```

Alternatively, the allocation/creation flow should avoid writing `ref:none` into TODO for the normal “ID first, brief later, issue-sync later” path.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**:

```bash
TASK_TITLE="Patch Crawl4AI live runner validation and browser recovery"
output=$(~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/planning-commit-helper.sh next-id --title "$TASK_TITLE")
# Parse TASK_ID/TASK_REF from output, then create TODO entry with ref:none and a worker-ready brief.
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper.sh push tNNN --repo OWNER/REPO
```

**Actual output**:

```text
[plan] Allocated tNNN (none)
TASK_ID=tNNN
TASK_REF=none
TASK_OFFLINE=false

[INFO] Processing 1 task(s) for push to OWNER/REPO
[SUCCESS] Created #NNNN: tNNN: Patch Crawl4AI live runner validation and browser recovery
[INFO] Push complete: 1 created, 0 skipped
```

After sync, the TODO line changed from:

```text
- [ ] tNNN ... ref:none logged:YYYY-MM-DD
```

to:

```text
- [ ] tNNN ... ref:none ref:GH#NNNN logged:YYYY-MM-DD
```

Manual workaround was required:

```text
ref:none ref:GH#NNNN -> ref:GH#NNNN
```

**Expected output**:

After `issue-sync-helper.sh push tNNN` creates the issue, the TODO line should contain only:

```text
ref:GH#NNNN
```

**Causal code**:

Observed in the deployed scripts for aidevops v3.31.19:

- `planning-commit-helper.sh` `_next_task_id_run_claim`, around lines 373-383: calls `claim-task-id.sh` with `--title` and only passes `--description` when provided.
- `planning-commit-helper.sh` `_next_task_id_parse_output`, around lines 412-441: maps `ref=none` to `TASK_REF=none`.
- `claim-task-id.sh` `create_github_issue`, around lines 556-563: if no description and no brief/body can be composed, issue creation is skipped and the secured ID is retained.
- `claim-task-id.sh` `_main_output_results`, around lines 1061-1088: emits `ref=none` when no issue was created and not offline.
- `issue-sync-lib.sh` `add_gh_ref_to_todo`, around lines 976-984: idempotence check only looks for existing `ref:GH#`, not `ref:none`.
- `issue-sync-lib.sh` `add_gh_ref_to_todo`, around lines 996-1009: inserts `ref:GH#NNNN` before `logged:` or appends it, leaving `ref:none` intact.

**Call-site sweep**:

`issue-sync-lib.sh` centralizes TODO ref management in `add_gh_ref_to_todo(...)` and `fix_gh_ref_in_todo(...)`. `issue-sync-helper.sh push` uses this path when creating or finding refs. The observed behavior is therefore likely shared by any delayed issue creation path that starts with a `ref:none` TODO token.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. In any managed project repo, run `planning-commit-helper.sh next-id --title "Some task"` before creating a brief or passing a description.
2. Observe `TASK_REF=none`.
3. Add a TODO line for that task containing `ref:none` and create a worker-ready brief.
4. Run `issue-sync-helper.sh push tNNN --repo OWNER/REPO`.
5. Observe that TODO now contains both `ref:none` and `ref:GH#NNNN`.

## Workarounds Applied

- Manually edited TODO to replace `ref:none ref:GH#NNNN` with `ref:GH#NNNN`.
- Committed and pushed a follow-up cleanup commit after the issue-sync-created issue existed.

## Suggested Investigation / Fix Options

Please treat these as considerations rather than a prescribed patch.

### Option A: Normalize in `add_gh_ref_to_todo(...)`

When adding a GitHub ref to a task line, replace an existing `ref:none` placeholder on that same task line, outside code fences, instead of inserting a second ref.

Possible behavior:

- If line has `ref:GH#same`, no-op.
- If line has `ref:GH#different`, keep existing behavior or route to `fix_gh_ref_in_todo(...)`/reconcile; do not silently overwrite without evidence.
- If line has `ref:none` and no `ref:GH#`, replace exactly that token with `ref:GH#NNNN`.
- If line has no `ref:` at all, insert before `logged:` as today.

### Option B: Avoid emitting/writing `ref:none` in normal `/new-task` delayed-issue flow

The documented `/new-task` flow allocates first and creates the brief later. If issue creation cannot happen until after the brief exists, the docs/helper could use an explicit pending state that is not a TODO `ref:` token, for example `TASK_REF=` empty or `TASK_REF=pending`, and only write a `ref:` field once a tracker issue exists.

This may be more invasive because callers likely already understand `ref:none`.

### Option C: Teach validators/sync status to detect multiple `ref:` tokens

Add a warning/failure for active TODO task lines containing more than one `ref:` token, especially `ref:none ref:GH#...`. This would catch future regressions even if the normalizer misses a path.

## Landmines / Second-Order Risks

- Do not blindly replace `ref:none` globally. TODO.md contains examples and code fences; existing helpers already try to operate outside code fences and should keep doing so.
- Do not replace `ref:none` on unrelated lines or notes. The change should target the exact task line for the task being synced.
- Preserve non-GitHub platforms. If GitLab refs are supported, analogous `ref:none -> ref:GL#NNNN` handling may be needed in the shared ref helper rather than GitHub-only code.
- Preserve offline/no-issue semantics. `ref:none` may be intentional for tasks where issue creation is deliberately skipped, offline, or pending. It should only be replaced when a concrete issue number has been created/found.
- Do not silently overwrite an existing real `ref:GH#old` with `ref:GH#new`; mismatches should remain a reconcile/fix path with evidence.
- Be careful with `logged:` insertion order. The current helper inserts refs before `logged:`; replacing `ref:none` should not duplicate or reorder unrelated proof fields unexpectedly.
- Consider concurrency. `issue-sync-helper.sh push` edits TODO after remote issue creation; if two sessions are creating/syncing nearby tasks, conflict-safe TODO updates still matter.
- Consider the command contract. `/new-task` currently tells agents to allocate before creating the mandatory brief. If the preferred path cannot create a GH issue until the brief exists, either the docs or helper should make that delayed-issue state explicit so agents do not assume `TASK_REF=GH#...` is guaranteed.

## Environment

- aidevops version: 3.31.19
- Latest version: 3.31.19
- AI assistant: OpenCode
- OS: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- Shell: bash 5.2.21
- gh CLI: 2.95.0
- Working repo: private project repo, sanitized

## Additional Context

A search found a related but distinct closed duplicate, #21736, about stale GH refs leaking in `claim-task-id.sh` output. This report is narrower/different: `ref=none` appears legitimate after ID-only allocation, but later issue sync appends a real ref without consuming the placeholder.

The user-facing friction was significant because it looked like a broader `/new-task` or issue-creation failure, even though the task ID, issue, and brief were all eventually valid after manual TODO cleanup.

Since `set -euo pipefail` is enabled, any failure in a pipeline (such as `jq` failing to parse invalid JSON) will cause the script to immediately terminate. If `gh api` succeeds but returns invalid JSON (e.g., an HTML error page or corrupted response), the downstream `jq` calls in `cmd_dispatch` will crash the script.

To prevent this, we should validate that the fetched payload is indeed valid JSON before returning it from `_fetch_comment`. Additionally, to ensure downstream consumers do not break, the function should output an empty JSON object (`{}`) on failure rather than returning a non-zero exit code or empty string. We should also avoid suppressing stderr (e.g., avoiding `2>&1` or `2>/dev/null`) so that any parsing errors remain visible for debugging.

```suggestion

		_log "dispatch: comment ${comment_id} on #${issue_number} returned invalid JSON — skipping"
		_mark_comment_skipped "$responded_file" "$comment_id" "invalid JSON"
		printf '{}'
		return 0
	fi

	printf '%s\n' "$comment_json"
	return 0
```

2. Avoid suppressing stderr with `2>/dev/null` on commands that parse configuration files or other inputs (e.g., `jq`), as it can hide syntax errors and make debugging difficult.

title: circuit-breaker-meta-filer.sh: body text creates circular blocked-by deadlock between meta-issue and original
body:
## Description

`circuit-breaker-meta-filer.sh` generates meta-issue body text containing both `blocked-by` and `#NNN` on the same line. `_blocked_by_extract_nums()` in `pulse-dep-graph.sh` then interprets `#NNN` on a `blocked-by` line as a dependency — so the meta-issue believes it's blocked by the very original it's supposed to unblock.

This creates a circular deadlock: original is blocked-by meta (GitHub label applied by filer), meta is blocked-by original (body fallback parsing). Neither can be dispatched.

## Expected Behavior

Meta-issue body should not produce false `blocked-by` references. Only the explicitly applied GitHub `blocked-by` label on the original issue should control dependency direction.

## Reproducer

**Symptom** (observed on Majowka/mesh-manager#1214 — meta for #48):

```
is_blocked_by_unresolved: #1214 native blockedBy lookup unavailable — checking body fallback
is_blocked_by_unresolved: #1214 blocked by #48 (live: open) — skipping dispatch
Dispatch_max: #1214 (Majowka/mesh-manager) blocked:blocked_by_unresolved benign dispatch block
```

**Causal code**:

Two lines in `circuit-breaker-meta-filer.sh` produce `blocked-by` + `#${issue_number}` on the same line:

```bash
# Line 290
The original (#${issue_number}) gets a \`blocked-by\` label pointing at this meta-issue...

# Line 379
3. PR merge automatically removes the meta \`blocked-by\` label from #${issue_number} via \`_unblock_circuit_breaker_meta_original\`.
```

`_blocked_by_extract_nums()` in `pulse-dep-graph.sh:663-669` extracts `#NNN` from any line containing `[Bb]locked[- ][Bb]y`:

```bash
_blocked_by_extract_nums() {
    local body="$1"
    local blocker_lines
    blocker_lines=$(printf '%s' "$body" | grep -ioE '[Bb]locked[- ][Bb]y[^[:cntrl:]]*' || true)
    printf '%s' "$blocker_lines" | grep -oE '#[0-9]+' | grep -oE '[0-9]+' || true
    return 0
}
```

**Call-site sweep:**

```
rg "blocked.by.*#" .agents/scripts/circuit-breaker-meta-filer.sh
.agents/scripts/circuit-breaker-meta-filer.sh:290: The original (#${issue_number}) gets a \`blocked-by\` label...
.agents/scripts/circuit-breaker-meta-filer.sh:379: 3. PR merge automatically removes the meta \`blocked-by\` label from #${issue_number}...
```

## Workarounds Applied

None — the deadlock was discovered during a pulse diagnostic session before any worker attempted dispatch of the meta-issue.

## Fix

Rephrase lines 290 and 379 in `circuit-breaker-meta-filer.sh` so `#${issue_number}` does not appear after `blocked-by` on the same line:

- **Line 290**: Move `#${issue_number}` before the `blocked-by` token.
- **Line 379**: Restructure to `... removes the meta \`blocked-by\` label (applied to #${issue_number}) via ...`

And/or harden `_blocked_by_extract_nums()` in `pulse-dep-graph.sh` to ignore `blocked-by` references inside backtick-quoted text and code-fence blocks, reducing false-positive surface for all body-generated blocked-by markers.

## Environment

- aidevops version: 3.31.25
- AI Assistant: OpenCode
- OS: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- Shell: bash 5.2.21(1)-release
- gh CLI: gh version 2.89.0

<!-- aidevops:sig -->
---

title: headless-runtime-model.sh _choose_model_auto() does not consult oauth-pool.json cooldown before dispatch
body:
## Description

`_choose_model_auto()` in `headless-runtime-model.sh` selects a model for pulse dispatch
by checking `provider_auth_available()` (credential presence) and `model_backoff_active()`
(rate-limit backoff DB), but it **never consults `oauth-pool.json`** for provider-level
cooldowns. When an OpenAI ChatGPT Plus account exhausts its session quota (~5h rolling
window), the cooldown is correctly recorded in `oauth-pool.json` either by:

- `provider-quota-monitor.sh` checking via `chatgpt.com/backend-api/wham/usage`, or
- `openai-provider-auth.mjs:handleOpenAIUsageLimit()` after a real 429 at fetch time

However, `_choose_model_auto()` still selects `openai/gpt-5.5` because:

1. `model-availability.db` shows OpenAI as `healthy` — the OAuth probe path
   (`model-availability-probe-lib.sh:429`) skips HTTP probing entirely when
   `resolve_api_key()` returns `oauth-refresh-available`, so quota exhaustion is
   never detected.
2. `provider_backoff` in `headless-runtime/state.db` has no entry for gpt-5.5
   (backoff is written only after canary failures or explicit 429 handling, neither
   of which fires when the probe skips HTTP).

The `oauth-pool.mjs:isAvailableAccount()` and `openai-provider-auth.mjs:isUnavailableAccount()`
functions exist and correctly check `cooldownUntil`, but they only run at fetch runtime
— by then the dispatch has already started a worker with `--initial-model openai/gpt-5.5`,
wasting a slot.

## Expected Behavior

`_choose_model_auto()` should check `oauth-pool.json` for active cooldowns on the
OpenAI account before selecting `openai/gpt-5.5` (or any OpenAI model). If the
account is on cooldown, skip OpenAI models and fall through the custom routing
chain (e.g., to `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6`).

## Reproducer

**Symptom** (observed during reporting session):

```
bash headless-runtime-helper.sh run --role worker --tier sonnet
  --initial-model openai/gpt-5.5 --agent Build+
  ...
  opencode run -m openai/gpt-5.5 ...
```

Multiple workers dispatched with `--initial-model openai/gpt-5.5` despite
`oauth-pool.json` already having:

```json
{
  "openai": [{
    "email": "user@example.com",
    "status": "rate-limited",
    "cooldownUntil": 1783041302000
  }]
}
```

**Expected dispatch model**: `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6` (the next model in the
custom routing fallback chain for the `sonnet` tier).

## Diagnostics from observing session

```
# oauth-pool.json had cooldown set, but dispatch ignored it
$ provider-quota-monitor.sh status
[openai] user@example.com
  Status: rate-limited
  Usage: 100% (session quota)
  Cooldown until: 2026-07-03 03:15 UTC
  Cooldown remaining: 176m

# model-availability.db still showed healthy (OAuth probe skips HTTP)
openai|healthy|0|0|OAuth refresh available|0|...

# no backoff for gpt-5.5 in headless-runtime state
$ sqlite3 headless-runtime/state.db "SELECT * FROM provider_backoff WHERE model='openai/gpt-5.5';"
(empty)
```

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure an OpenAI ChatGPT Plus account via OAuth (`auth.json`)
2. Use the account until session quota is exhausted (~5h rolling window)
3. Configure custom routing (`custom/configs/model-routing-table.json`)
   with fallback models (e.g., Anthropic Claude Sonnet)
4. Pulse dispatches a worker with `tier:sonnet` (no explicit `tier:*` label)
5. Observe: worker launches with `--initial-model openai/gpt-5.5` despite cooldown
6. Worker session gets 429 or usage-limit at first API call

## Workarounds Applied

1. Set `AIDEVOPS_HEADLESS_PROVIDER_ALLOWLIST=anthropic` — prevents pulse from
   considering OpenAI at all (also blocks valid OpenAI slots when quota is healthy).
2. Monitor cooldown manually and `unset`/clear only when quota resets.

## Causal code

`_choose_model_auto()` in `headless-runtime-model.sh:270-326`:

```bash
_choose_model_auto() {
    ...
```

title: workflow: avoid PR branch updates that restart active CI
body:
## What

Improve the generic aidevops PR workflow so agents avoid unnecessary CI restarts caused by updating a pull request branch while required checks are already queued or running.

## Why

When a pull request branch is updated from its base branch during active CI, GitHub starts a new check suite for the new head SHA. This can waste runner time, invalidate nearly-complete checks, force repeated polling, and delay auto-merge even when the PR is already approved and mergeable. The framework should make the cheaper path the default: keep the current head stable, enable auto-merge when safe, and only update the branch when the platform or merge state requires it.

## Scope

This should be implemented generically for any repository and any base branch name. Do not hard-code project names, owner names, repository names, or branch names.

## Desired behavior

### 1. Pre-update guard for PR branches

Before any helper, loop, worker, or interactive flow updates a PR branch from its base branch, check the current PR state:

- current PR head SHA
- mergeability / conflict state
- whether branch protection requires the branch to be up to date
- pending or in-progress required checks for the current head SHA
- whether auto-merge is already enabled

If required checks are pending or in progress and the PR is not conflicted/out-of-date by ruleset requirement, do not update the branch. Instead report that updating now would restart checks and recommend waiting for the current run or enabling auto-merge.

### 2. Auto-merge-first path

When a PR is approved, mergeable, not draft, and not blocked by requested changes, security, data-loss, migration, or maintainer-review labels, prefer enabling auto-merge rather than repeatedly polling or refreshing the branch.

The loop should then stop active polling unless a terminal failed required check appears.

### 3. Head-SHA-aware failure diagnosis

Before diagnosing or fixing a failed CI check, verify the failed check belongs to the current PR head SHA. If the failure is stale, ignore it and continue monitoring the latest head.

### 4. Stale-run cleanup guidance

When a PR has active runs for older head SHAs, surface a safe recommendation to cancel superseded runs. Only cancel automatically when the helper can prove the run belongs to the same PR/branch, is not the latest head SHA, and is still queued or in progress.

### 5. Merge queue guidance

If a repository requires testing the exact merge result, prefer merge queue or platform-native queued merge behavior over mutating the PR branch repeatedly.

## Likely implementation areas

Start by inspecting these generic workflow/helper areas and adjust based on the current code layout:

- `.agents/workflows/git-workflow.md`
- `.agents/workflows/pr.md`
- `.agents/workflows/postflight.md`
- `.agents/reference/ci-gate-policy.md`
- `.agents/reference/worker-diagnostics.md`
- `.agents/scripts/interactive-session-helper*.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-*.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/loop-*.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/shared-gh-wrappers*.sh`
- any helper that runs `gh pr merge --auto`, `gh pr update-branch`, `git merge <base>`, or equivalent PR branch refresh logic

## Implementation notes

- Use GitHub API/CLI data keyed by PR number and head SHA; do not rely on check names alone.
- Treat queued and in-progress checks as non-failures.
- Avoid noisy comments. Prefer local/tool output unless the worker is explicitly assigned to a PR/issue thread.
- Keep the guard fail-open for unsupported hosting providers, but record a clear warning in helper output.
- If a deterministic guard is added, include tests for: pending checks block branch update, conflict allows update, stale failed check is ignored, current failed check is diagnosed, auto-merge is enabled without branch refresh, and superseded run cancellation only targets older head SHAs.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] PR branch update helpers warn/block when required checks are already pending or in progress for the current head and no conflict/out-of-date requirement exists.
- [ ] Approved/mergeable PRs use auto-merge before repeated polling or branch refresh.
- [ ] CI failure diagnosis ignores stale failures from older PR head SHAs.
- [ ] Superseded run cancellation is either implemented safely or documented as an explicit operator action with exact guard conditions.
- [ ] Documentation explains the trade-off between branch refresh, auto-merge, and merge queue without naming any specific project or base branch.
- [ ] Tests or fixture-backed helper checks cover the new decision logic.

## Verification

```bash
# Adjust to the touched files and helper tests.
shellcheck .agents/scripts/*.sh
pnpm test
```

If the implementation changes shell helpers, run the nearest existing shell helper tests and add/extend tests for the decision logic.

title: maintainer-gate-reusable.yml: gh api .../comments calls missing --paginate, causing NMR loop on issues with 30+ comments
body:
## Description

`maintainer-gate-reusable.yml` has 9 calls to `gh api repos/.../issues/N/comments` without `--paginate`. The GitHub Issues API returns comments paginated (30/page by default). When an issue accumulates 30+ comments (e.g., after repeated dispatch attempts + auto-approve cycles), the marker comment `<!-- aidevops-signed-approval -->` lands on page 2+ and is never found by the maintainer gate.

This causes a tight loop:
1. Auto-approve posts `<!-- aidevops-signed-approval -->` + removes NMR label
2. maintainer-gate fires on `unlabeled` event, checks comments → sees only page 1 (30 dispatch claims) → no marker found
3. Re-applies `needs-maintainer-review` label
4. Next pulse cycle: auto-approve sees NMR → GOTO 1

Each cycle adds another dispatch-comment, making the issue grow past 30 comments faster and the window for finding the marker narrower.

## Expected Behavior

Adding `--paginate` to all `gh api .../comments` calls so the marker is found regardless of how many comments the issue has. A comment posted before the label removal should be visible to the workflow that fires on that removal.

## Affected Locations

File: `.github/workflows/maintainer-gate-reusable.yml` — all 9 `gh api .../comments` calls lack `--paginate`:

| Line | Variable | Purpose |
|------|----------|---------|
| 225 | `SIGNED_APPROVAL` | PR signed approval check |
| 445 | `NON_MAINT_COMMENTS` | Non-maintainer comments filter |
| 570 | `SIGNED_APPROVAL` | Issue signed approval check |
| 585 | `EXISTING` | Label-protection-notice dedup |
| 786 | `NON_MAINT_COMMENTS_J3` | Non-maintainer comments filter (Job 3) |
| 900 | `SIGNED_APPROVAL` | PR signed approval check (Job 4) |
| 915 | `EXISTING` | PR label-protection-notice dedup |
| 1075 | `EXISTING` | PR comment dedup |

## Reproducer

**Symptom command** (observed on Majowka/mesh-manager #1336):

```bash
# Without --paginate — returns 0 markers (page 1 has 30 dispatch comments)
gh api repos/Majowka/mesh-manager/issues/1336/comments \
  --jq '[.[] | select(.body | contains("aidevops-signed-approval"))] | length'
# → 0

# With --paginate — returns 18 markers (spread across pages)
gh api repos/Majowka/mesh-manager/issues/1336/comments --paginate \
  --jq '[.[] | select(.body | contains("aidevops-signed-approval"))] | length'
# → 18
```

**Workflow log evidence** (Majowka/mesh-manager maintainer-gate run for #1343, 2026-07-03T09:07):

```
Label 'needs-maintainer-review' removed from issue #1343 by katarzynacc
DENIED: No signed approval found — re-applying label (actor: katarzynacc)
GraphQL: Unable to create comment because issue is locked (addComment)
```

The signed approval comment was posted 15 seconds before the label removal (comment ID 4874609914 at 09:07:01Z, label removed at ~09:07:16Z), but the workflow did not find it because it was on page 2+.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Have any issue accumulate >30 comments (dispatch claims, status toggles, etc.)
2. Pulse auto-approve posts `<!-- aidevops-signed-approval -->` and removes NMR
3. maintainer-gate workflow fires on `unlabeled`
4. Workflow reads comments without `--paginate`, sees only first 30 → marker not found
5. Workflow re-applies `needs-maintainer-review`
6. Cycle repeats every pulse cycle until issue has 60, 90, 120... comments

## Workarounds Applied

- Manual `sudo aidevops approve issue NNN` — uses cryptographic approval path, not the comment-marker check. The issue then carries `ever-NMR` flag but auto-approve cannot auto-clear it because `_nmr_applied_by_maintainer` detects the cryptographic approval and preserves NMR as intentional.

## Environment

- aidevops: 3.31.33
- gh: 2.89.0
- OS: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- Shell: bash 5.2.21

## Additional Context

Current HEAD of `maintainer-gate-reusable.yml` is `989dc0f` (2026-07-03). All 9 callsites were last touched in that commit.

The pinned copy in downstream repos (e.g., `Majowka/.github@88fceecc`) inherits the same bug.

title: pulse-cleanup: 6h dirty worktree rule is dead code after GH#23677
body:
## Description

The 6-hour dirty worktree cleanup rule in `pulse-cleanup.sh:_evaluate_worktree_removal()` is dead code. It evaluates to "eligible" for 0-commit dirty worktrees >6h old, but is never reached because `_pc_assert_no_uncommitted_work()` (added by GH#23677 / PR #23678) blocks **any** dirty worktree removal unconditionally before the evaluate result is acted upon.

**Effect**: Orphaned 0-commit dirty worktrees accumulate permanently — Pulse's Pass 2 cleanup never removes them, regardless of age.

## Reproducer

**Symptom**: 17+ orphan worktrees in mesh-manager repo, all with 0 commits + 1 dirty file + age 1-5 days, listed every cycle in `pulse-state.txt` under "Hygiene Anomalies" but never cleaned.

**Actual flow** (call chain):

```
_cleanup_single_worktree()
  → _evaluate_worktree_removal()
    → 6h rule matches: "0 commits, 1 dirty files, age 5d"
    → returns 0 (eligible)
  → _pc_assert_no_uncommitted_work()
    → dirty_count > 0 → "refusing permanent removal (GH#23677)"
    → returns 1 (BLOCKED)
  → cleanup never proceeds
```

**Expected**: Either the 6h rule is reachable (and removes dirty worktrees after 6h grace), or it is removed as dead code.

## Causal code

Two locations in `pulse-cleanup.sh`:

1. **6h rule** (`_evaluate_worktree_removal`, ~line 743):
```bash
elif [[ "$commits_ahead" -eq 0 && "$dirty_count" -gt 0 && "$wt_age_secs" -ge "$age_6h" ]]; then
    echo "0 commits, ${dirty_count} dirty files, age $((wt_age_secs / 3600))h"
    return 0  # ← cleanable, but never reached
```

2. **Guard** (`_pc_assert_no_uncommitted_work`, ~line 1081):
```bash
if [[ "$dirty_count" -gt 0 ]]; then
    echo "... refusing permanent removal (GH#23677)"
    return 1  # ← always blocks dirty worktrees before evaluate result used
```

## Call-site sweep

All locations where `_pc_assert_no_uncommitted_work` is called — confirming it blocks ALL dirty removal paths:

```bash
# pulse-cleanup.sh line ~1395 — called after _evaluate_worktree_removal
if ! _pc_assert_no_uncommitted_work "$wt_path_age" "$wt_branch_age" "$dirty_count" ...; then
    return 1
fi
```

## History

- **GH#23677** / PR #23678 added `_pc_assert_no_uncommitted_work` as defence-in-depth to prevent the 30min fast-path from destroying dirty worktrees. The fix correctly added `dirty_count -eq 0` to the fast-path.
- **Side effect**: The defence-in-depth guard is placed *after* `_evaluate_worktree_removal` in `_cleanup_single_worktree`, so it blocks **all** dirty worktree removal — including the 6h rule which was designed for "worker died mid-edit" scenarios.
- The 6h rule in `_evaluate_worktree_removal` was not removed, creating dead code.

## Options to resolve

1. **Remove the 6h rule** from `_evaluate_worktree_removal` — it's unreachable, dead code invites confusion during future maintenance
2. **Add a long timeout to the guard** — after 7+ days, allow dirty worktree removal anyway (crashed worker, not interactive session)
3. **Trash instead of permanent removal** — if dirty, move to Trash instead of `rm -rf`, giving the user a recovery path

Option 1 or 2 + 3 would be the cleanest resolution.

## Files to modify

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-cleanup.sh` — `_evaluate_worktree_removal()` ~line 743, `_pc_assert_no_uncommitted_work()` ~line 1081

## Verification

```bash
shellcheck -x .agents/scripts/pulse-cleanup.sh
# Confirm 6h-rule branches are either removed or reachable
# Run existing worktree cleanup tests
```

## Workarounds Applied

This session: none — the user noticed orphans accumulating and asked why. Manual cleanup would be `git worktree remove --force` on each orphan.

## Environment

- **aidevops version**: 3.31.33
- **OS**: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- **Shell**: bash 5.2.21(1)-release
- **gh CLI**: 2.89.0

## Siblings

- GH#23677 — original fix that introduced the dirty-content-protect guard (merged)
- GH#23678 — original fix PR

title: model-availability-helper.sh doesn't read oauth-pool.json cooldowns, causing split-brain availability state
body:
## Description

`model-availability-helper.sh` does not read `oauth-pool.json` cooldowns when determining provider availability. It checks API key presence and optionally performs HTTP probes, but never consults the cooldown state managed by `provider-quota-monitor.sh` and recorded in `oauth-pool.json`.

This causes `fallback-chain-helper.sh` (which delegates to `model-availability-helper.sh check <provider>`) to report a provider as "available" even when that provider has an active rate-limit cooldown.

**Impact**: During the ~15-minute gap between quota exhaustion and `provider-quota-monitor.sh` detection, or when `fallback-chain-helper.sh` is used directly for model resolution, exhausted providers may be selected because the availability check doesn't see the cooldown.

**Contrast with pulse-capacity.sh**: `pulse-capacity.sh` and `pulse-fast-fail.sh` DO read `oauth-pool.json` directly and respect cooldowns. This creates an inconsistency where different parts of the framework have different views of provider availability.

## Expected Behavior

`model-availability-helper.sh check <provider>` should:
1. Check `oauth-pool.json` for active cooldowns (where `cooldownUntil` > current timestamp and `status == "rate-limited"`)
2. Return exit code 2 (rate-limited) if cooldown is active
3. Skip HTTP probe and use cached "unavailable" status during cooldown period

This would align `model-availability-helper.sh` behavior with `pulse-capacity.sh` and create a single source of truth for provider cooldown state.

## Reproducer

**Symptom commands**:

```bash
# OAuth pool shows OpenAI rate-limited with active cooldown
jq -r '.openai[0] | "status=\(.status), cooldownUntil=\(.cooldownUntil)"' ~/.aidevops/oauth-pool.json
# Output: status=rate-limited, cooldownUntil=1783102501000

# Current timestamp
date +%s000
# Output: 1783084888000

# Cooldown is active (cooldownUntil > now), but...
model-availability-helper.sh check openai
# Output: [WARNING] openai: cached key-invalid
# Exit code: 3 (no-key)
```

**Actual output**:

```
[WARNING] openai: cached key-invalid
```

Exit code 3 (treated as "unavailable" but for wrong reason - should be exit 2 for rate-limited)

**Expected output**:

```
[WARNING] openai: rate-limited until 2026-07-03T18:15:01Z
```

Exit code 2 (rate-limited), and fallback-chain-helper should skip to next model in chain.

**Comparison with pulse-capacity**:

```bash
# pulse-capacity DOES respect the cooldown
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-capacity.sh provider-available openai
# Exit code: 0 (considers OAuth auth.json, not oauth-pool cooldowns - different bug)
```

**Call-site sweep**:

```bash
# Scripts that read oauth-pool.json (work correctly)
grep -l "oauth-pool.json" ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/*.sh
# pulse-capacity.sh, pulse-fast-fail.sh, oauth-pool-*.sh

# Scripts that delegate to model-availability-helper (don't see cooldowns)
grep -l "model-availability-helper" ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/*.sh  
# fallback-chain-helper.sh, pulse-wrapper-config.sh
```

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure OpenAI OAuth account (ChatGPT Plus) via `~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json`
2. Exhaust session quota (~5h rolling window)
3. Wait for `provider-quota-monitor.sh` to detect exhaustion and set cooldown in `oauth-pool.json`:
   ```json
   {
     "openai": [{
       "email": "user@example.com",
       "status": "rate-limited",
       "cooldownUntil": 1783102501000
     }]
   }
   ```
4. Run `model-availability-helper.sh check openai`
5. Observe: Returns exit 3 (no-key) instead of exit 2 (rate-limited)
6. Run `fallback-chain-helper.sh resolve sonnet`
7. Observe: May still try openai/gpt-5.5 because availability check doesn't see cooldown

## Workarounds Applied

1. **Used `AIDEVOPS_HEADLESS_PROVIDER_ALLOWLIST=anthropic`** - prevents considering OpenAI at all (too aggressive, blocks valid OpenAI use when quota is healthy)
2. **Relied on pulse-capacity.sh direct checks** - works for pulse dispatch but doesn't help interactive fallback-chain use

## Causal code

`model-availability-helper.sh` has no code to read `oauth-pool.json`:

```bash
grep -n "oauth-pool" ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/model-availability-helper.sh
# (no output - file never references oauth-pool.json)
```

The `is_model_available()` function in `fallback-chain-helper.sh:75-119` delegates to `model-availability-helper.sh check <provider>` which only checks:
- API key presence (via `resolve_api_key()`)
- HTTP probe status (cached in SQLite DB)

It never consults `oauth-pool.json` cooldown state.

## Siblings

**Related (but different) issue #26392 (closed)**: Fixed `headless-runtime-model.sh:_choose_model_auto()` not consulting oauth-pool.json. That was the dispatch code path. This issue is about the availability-check code path used by `fallback-chain-helper.sh`.

**Potential sibling (not filed)**: `model-availability-probe-lib.sh:429` skips HTTP probes entirely for OAuth providers (returns "oauth-refresh-available" marker). This means quota exhaustion is never detected by the probe. However, with the cooldown integration proposed here, the cooldown would be set by `provider-quota-monitor.sh` or runtime 429 handlers, so the probe skip is less critical.

## Environment

- **aidevops version**: 3.31.33
- **Latest version**: 3.31.33
- **Install method**: unknown (~/.local/bin/aidevops)
- **AI Assistant**: OpenCode
- **OS**: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- **Shell**: bash 5.2.21(1)-release
- **Working repo**: <webapp> (develop)
- **gh CLI**: gh version 2.89.0 (2026-03-26)

## Additional Context

**Memory recall** shows issue #26392 fixed the similar problem in `headless-runtime-model.sh` (closed 2026-07-02). This issue addresses the parallel gap in `model-availability-helper.sh`.

**Discovery check**: No recent commits to `model-availability-helper.sh` in the last week touch cooldown logic (this was never implemented).

**Architecture note**: The framework currently has two separate systems for checking provider availability:
1. `pulse-capacity.sh` + `pulse-fast-fail.sh` - read oauth-pool.json directly (used by pulse dispatch)
2. `model-availability-helper.sh` - doesn't read oauth-pool.json (used by fallback-chain and interactive resolution)

This creates a split-brain where different parts of the framework see different availability states. Fixing this would create a single source of truth.

title: bug: worker-activity-watchdog hard kill timeout never triggers when output file grows
body:
## Summary

Worker-activity-watchdog hard kill timeout (`HARD_KILL_SECONDS=1500` / 25 min) never triggers when output file grows continuously. Workers can run for 3+ hours instead of being killed at the configured limit.

## Reproducer

1. Dispatch a worker task that produces slow, continuous output (e.g., long-running tool call like `gh run view --log` on a large workflow)
2. Observe output file growing ≥1 byte every 10 minutes
3. Wait past `HARD_KILL_SECONDS` threshold (25 minutes)
4. **Expected**: Worker killed at 25 min with `watchdog_hard_kill` result
5. **Actual**: Worker continues indefinitely (observed: 227 minutes on managed repo issue #1369)

## Evidence

Managed repo issue #1369, worker PID 678564:
- Elapsed: **13,641 seconds (227 minutes)** before kill
- Expected kill: **1,500 seconds (25 minutes)**
- Output file grew continuously during `gh run view --log` deadlock
- Watchdog log shows **zero** `stall_deferred` events before final kill
- No hard kill timeout triggered despite exceeding limit by 9× factor

Relevant logs:
- `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-dispatch.log` - lifecycle confirms 13,641s runtime
- `~/.aidevops/logs/headless-runtime-metrics.jsonl` - metrics show `watchdog_stall_killed` at 13,644s
- `~/.aidevops/logs/worker-failure-excerpts/issue-1369-*.log` - 64K excerpt showing 203-min gap

## Root Cause

`worker-activity-watchdog.sh:730` - hard kill check is inside `_monitor_handle_confirmed_stall()`, which only executes after stall detection:

```bash
# Line ~450: Main loop
if [[ "$current_size" -gt "$last_size" ]]; then
    _MONITOR_STALL_SECONDS=0  # Reset stall counter
    # Hard kill check NEVER reached - not in this branch
fi

# Line ~600: Stall branch (only if stall_seconds >= 600)
if [[ "$_MONITOR_STALL_SECONDS" -ge "$stall_threshold" ]]; then
    _monitor_handle_confirmed_stall  # Contains hard kill check at line 730
fi
```

**Logic flaw**: If output grows ≥1 byte per 10 minutes, stall counter resets to 0 → stall never reaches 600s → confirmed_stall never called → **hard kill check never executed**.

## Expected Behavior

`HARD_KILL_SECONDS` is an **absolute timeout** - "kill after 25 min total elapsed regardless of output growth". Should trigger even during healthy progress.

## Actual Behavior

Workers live indefinitely if output grows continuously, treating hard kill as "maximum stall duration" instead of "maximum total duration".

## Fix Approach

Move absolute hard kill check to **main loop** before stall detection branch:

```bash
# Check hard kill timeout FIRST (absolute elapsed time)
if [[ "$_MONITOR_ELAPSED_SECONDS" -ge "$HARD_KILL_SECONDS" ]]; then
    _monitor_handle_hard_kill_timeout
    return 1
fi

# Then check stall/progress logic
if [[ "$current_size" -gt "$last_size" ]]; then
    # Progress detected...
```

This ensures hard kill triggers at 25 min regardless of output behavior.

## Impact

- Zombie workers waste 3+ hours of compute on deadlocked tasks
- Circuit breaker delays accumulate (managed repo pulse stuck in ERROR for 5h)
- GitHub API budget consumed by runaway tool calls
- Observability/metrics skewed by outlier runtimes (227 min vs expected 25 min)

## Related

Secondary finding during investigation: OpenCode tool call timeout also failed - `gh run view --log` ran 203 minutes despite 120s timeout configuration. Should be tracked separately (possible OpenCode bug vs framework bug).

---

**Fingerprint**: `worker-activity-watchdog hard kill timeout never triggers when output file grows`

title: bug: review-bot-gate-helper.sh @tsv + bash read fails when .created_at is empty (reviews endpoint)
body:
## Description

`bot_has_real_review()` and `_classify_bot_state()` in `review-bot-gate-helper.sh` fail to detect bot reviews from the PR reviews API endpoint because the `@tsv` jq output produces a leading tab when the first field (`.created_at`) is null/absent, and bash `read` with `IFS=$'\t'` strips the leading IFS whitespace, causing all fields to shift left by one.

The result is `encoded` (base64 body) is always empty, the comment is skipped, the bot is classified as "non-review state", and the gate returns `WAITING` — permanently blocking merge for any PR where the only bot review comes via the reviews endpoint (which uses `.submitted_at`, not `.created_at`).

## Expected Behavior

When a known bot posts a real review (non-rate-limited, non-failure body) via the PR reviews endpoint, `bot_has_real_review()` should return true and the gate should pass.

## Reproducer

**Symptom command**:

```
review-bot-gate-helper.sh check 1436 Majowka/mesh-manager
```

**Actual output**:

```
non-review state (not rate-limited, not a real review): gemini-code-assist
WAITING
Bots posted non-review states that are not rate limits: gemini-code-assist 
Gate will keep polling; review_gate.rate_limit_behavior only applies to true rate-limit notices.
```

**Expected output**:

```
PASS
```

**Causal code**:

The jq filter at line 608 (and identical copy at line 1061):

```
[(.created_at // ""), (.updated_at // .submitted_at // .created_at // ""), (.body // "" | @base64)] | @tsv
```

For the PR reviews endpoint, `.created_at` is absent (only `.submitted_at` exists), so the array becomes `["", "2026-07-03T14:41:30Z", "BASE64..."]`. `@tsv` produces `\t2026-07-03T14:41:30Z\tBASE64...`.

Bash `read -r created_at updated_at encoded` with `IFS=$'\t'` strips the leading IFS tab, so:

- `created_at` gets `"2026-07-03T14:41:30Z"` (should be `""`)
- `updated_at` gets `"BASE64..."` (should be the date)
- `encoded` gets `""` (should be the base64 body)

Then `[[ -z "$encoded" ]] && continue` skips the comment entirely.

Introduced in commit `f751a02a99` (t2139, PR #19309, 2026-04-16).

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Have a PR with a review from a known bot (e.g. gemini-code-assist) posted via the reviews endpoint.
2. Run `review-bot-gate-helper.sh check <PR> <REPO>`.
3. Observe `WAITING` even though a real, settled review exists.
4. The gate stays `WAITING` permanently — no bot will re-post, so the PR is deadlocked.

## Workarounds Applied

- Add `skip-review-gate` label to the blocked PR to bypass the gate.

## Affected Locations

Two copies of the same jq filter:

| Line | Function |
|------|----------|
| 608 | `bot_has_real_review()` |
| 1061 | `_classify_bot_state()` |

## Fix

Change the first field expression from `(.created_at // "")` to `(.created_at // .submitted_at // "")` so it never produces an empty string:

```
[(.created_at // .submitted_at // ""), (.updated_at // .submitted_at // .created_at // ""), (.body // "" | @base64)] | @tsv
```

This makes the TSV output start with a non-empty timestamp, preventing the leading-IFS-tab stripping by bash `read`.

## Environment

- **aidevops version**: 3.31.35
- **OS**: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- **Shell**: bash 5.2.21(1)-release
- **gh CLI**: gh version 2.89.0 (2026-03-26)

If the `WRAPPER_STARTED` line is missing from the helper script, `grep` will exit with a non-zero status. Because `|| true` is used, this failure is ignored, and `wrapper_started_line` is left empty. This causes the subsequent check on line 41 (`[[ "$wrapper_started_line" != *"2>/dev/null"* ]]`) to silently pass, resulting in a false positive where a missing sentinel line is not detected.

To prevent this, we should add a guard clause to check if the variable is empty before using it, as its value is derived from an external command that could fail or produce no output. We can then call the script's `fail` function to abort the test if the variable is empty.

```suggestion
wrapper_started_line=$(grep -F "WRAPPER_STARTED" "$HELPER" | tail -n 1) || true
if [[ -z "$wrapper_started_line" ]]; then
  fail "WRAPPER_STARTED line not found in helper script"
fi
```

> To improve efficiency and maintainability, we can refactor `_merge_pr_ready_for_interactive_admin_bypass` in two ways:

> }

> This pull request introduces an interactive admin merge fallback mechanism in `full-loop-helper.sh merge --auto`. When a merge is blocked solely by review-required branch policies or self-approval rules, interactive maintainer sessions can automatically fall back to an `--admin` merge, provided that the PR is not a draft, has no changes requested, all status checks are passing, and any linked issue with `needs-maintainer-review` has been cleared. title: full-loop-helper.sh: missing create-pr alias for commit-and-pr causes unlabeled PRs and broken pulse fix-routing
body:
## Description

`full-loop-helper.sh` has a `commit-and-pr` subcommand but no `create-pr` alias. When a headless worker (AI) tries to create a PR, it naturally calls `full-loop-helper.sh create-pr` because that's the semantically obvious name. This fails with `[ERROR] Unknown command: create-pr`, and the worker falls back to raw `gh pr create` — which bypasses the framework wrapper and does NOT add the `origin:worker` label to the PR.

Without `origin:worker` on the PR, pulse's `_route_pr_to_fix_worker()` (pulse-merge-process.sh:1157) cannot route CHANGES_REQUESTED PRs to a fix worker. The PR remains stuck open with reviewDecision=CHANGES_REQUESTED, never dispatched for fixes.

## Expected Behavior

- `full-loop-helper.sh create-pr` should be an alias for `commit-and-pr`, OR
- The help text and error message should tell the user the correct command name
- Workers using `create-pr` should succeed and produce a properly labeled PR

## Reproducer

**Symptom command** (what the worker ran):

```
full-loop-helper.sh create-pr --issue 894 --title "feat: fix IDOR vulnerabilities in Bridge API" --body "..."
```

**Actual output**:

```
[ERROR] Unknown command: create-pr
Full Development Loop Orchestrator
Usage: full-loop-helper.sh <command> [options]
Commands:
  start "<prompt>"              Start a new development loop
  resume                        Resume from last phase
  status                        Show current loop state
  cancel                        Cancel active loop
  logs [N]                      Show last N log lines (default: 50)
  commit-and-pr --issue N --message "msg"  Stage, commit, rebase, push, create PR, post merge summary
```

**Worker fallback after error** (raw gh — missing label):

```
gh pr create --base develop --title "feat: fix IDOR vulnerabilities in Bridge API" --body-file /tmp/pr-body-894.md
```

**Consequence in pulse log** — PR skipped, never routed:

```
[pulse-wrapper] Merge pass: skipping PR #1514 — reviewDecision=CHANGES_REQUESTED
```

No `_route_pr_to_fix_worker` call because `origin:worker` is missing from PR labels.

**Causal code**:

full-loop-helper.sh:199-235 — has `commit-and-pr` but no `create-pr` alias:

```bash
commit-and-pr) cmd_commit_and_pr "$@" ;;
# No create-pr alias exists
```

Call-site sweep — worker expected `create-pr` because:
1. It's the natural name for "create a PR"

title: bug: _handle_changes_requested_review_gate skips thread remediation, routes directly to fix worker
body:
## Description

`_handle_changes_requested_review_gate()` in `pulse-merge.sh` calls `_route_pr_to_fix_worker()` directly for any non-CodeRabbit `CHANGES_REQUESTED` PR, bypassing the review-thread remediation path. The thread remediation (`_pulse_merge_maybe_dispatch_review_thread_remediation`) can answer threads, fix code, and resolve conversations — but it only fires after a failed merge attempt with "A conversation must be resolved". Since PRs with `reviewDecision=CHANGES_REQUESTED` never reach the merge attempt (the gate returns early at line 250), thread remediation is never triggered.

**Impact**: Every `origin:worker` PR with human CHANGES_REQUESTED gets closed and re-dispatched as a fresh worker, wasting tokens, losing PR context, and resetting CI. Many CHANGES_REQUESTED reviews could be addressed by the thread remediation worker (reply to threads, push fixes) without closing the PR.

## Expected Behavior

Before routing a CHANGES_REQUESTED PR to a fix worker (which closes the PR and re-dispatches), pulse should first attempt thread remediation. If remediation can resolve the threads (answer questions, push fixes), the PR stays open and can proceed to merge after the reviewer approves.

## Reproducer

**Observed in production**: PR #1514 in Majowka/mesh-manager had `reviewDecision=CHANGES_REQUESTED` from kamcio2603 with 5 specific fix requests. Pulse skipped merge (correct), but instead of trying thread remediation, called `_route_pr_to_fix_worker` which closed the PR, appended feedback to linked issue #894, and dispatched a brand new worker. The PR was lost; all CI + review context had to be rebuilt from scratch.

**Symptom command**:

```bash
# Pulse merge pass sees:
# PR #1514 has reviewDecision=CHANGES_REQUESTED, labels=origin:worker
```

**Actual pulse.log output**:

```
[pulse-merge] _handle_changes_requested_review_gate: CHANGES_REQUESTED
[pulse-wrapper] _dispatch_pr_fix_worker: routed review feedback from PR #1514 to issue #894
[pulse-wrapper] Merge pass: skipping PR #1514 — reviewDecision=CHANGES_REQUESTED
```

Note: no `review-thread remediation queued` log line appears. Thread remediation was never called.

**Expected output**:

```
[pulse-merge] review-thread remediation queued for PR #1514 after CHANGES_REQUESTED routing
# ... worker replies to threads, pushes fixes ...
# If reviewer approves → merge
# If reviewer still requests changes → _route_pr_to_fix_worker as fallback
```

**Causal code**:

`pulse-merge.sh:246-248` — the `else` branch after coderabbit-nits-ok check:
```bash
# No coderabbit-nits-ok label — route worker-authored PRs for fix
# dispatch and skip the merge (t2203: consolidated in helper).
_route_pr_to_fix_worker "$pr_number" "$repo_slug" "$linked_issue" "review" "$_cr_pr_labels" || true
echo "[pulse-wrapper] Merge pass: skipping PR #${pr_number} in ${repo_slug} — reviewDecision=CHANGES_REQUESTED" >>"$LOGFILE"
return 1
```

This calls `_route_pr_to_fix_worker` (which closes the PR + dispatches new worker) without ever calling `_pulse_merge_maybe_dispatch_review_thread_remediation` (which would try to resolve threads first).

Meanwhile `_pulse_merge_maybe_dispatch_review_thread_remediation` at `pulse-merge.sh:110-128` works correctly but is only called after a failed merge attempt at line 1215:
```bash
[[ "$merge_output" == *"A conversation must be resolved"* ]] || return 0
```

CHANGES_REQUESTED PRs never reach line 1215 because `_handle_changes_requested_review_gate` returns 1 at line 250, which propagates back through `_check_pr_merge_gates` → `_process_single_ready_pr` → merge attempt is never attempted.

**Call-site sweep** (both function references in pulse-merge.sh):
```
pulse-merge.sh:110  _pulse_merge_maybe_dispatch_review_thread_remediation() { ... }
pulse-merge.sh:248  _route_pr_to_fix_worker ...   # called from _handle_changes_requested_review_gate
pulse-merge.sh:1215 _pulse_merge_maybe_dispatch_review_thread_remediation ... # only called after failed merge
```

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Have an `origin:worker` PR with `reviewDecision=CHANGES_REQUESTED` from a human reviewer
2. Pulse runs its merge pass
3. `_handle_changes_requested_review_gate` fires at line 209
4. Reviewer is not CodeRabbit → no dismissal, falls through to line 246
5. `_route_pr_to_fix_worker` is called — PR is closed, feedback routed to issue, new worker dispatched
6. Thread remediation (`_pulse_merge_maybe_dispatch_review_thread_remediation`) is never called — no log entry for it

## Workarounds Applied

- Manually added `origin:worker` label to PR #1514 (it was missing due to separate bug #26533) so pulse could route it
- PR was closed and re-dispatched anyway — no way to keep the PR open and try to fix threads

## Suggested Implementation

**File**: `pulse-merge.sh`

**Location**: Inside `_handle_changes_requested_review_gate()`, at line 246-248, BEFORE calling `_route_pr_to_fix_worker`.

**Logic**:

```bash
# Before routing to fix worker, try thread remediation first
local repo_path=""
if repo_path="$(_pulse_merge_repo_path_for_slug "$repo_slug")"; then
    PR_REVIEW_THREAD_RESPONSE_INCLUDE_HUMAN=true \
        "$_PULSE_MERGE_DIR/pr-review-thread-response-scanner.sh" \
        dispatch-pr "$repo_slug" "$repo_path" "$pr_number" >>"$LOGFILE" 2>&1 || true
    echo "[pulse-merge] review-thread remediation queued for PR #${pr_number} in ${repo_slug} after CHANGES_REQUESTED routing" >>"$LOGFILE"
fi
# Fall through to _route_pr_to_fix_worker — if threads were resolved by the
# worker and the reviewer approves before the next pulse cycle, the review gate
# will clear and the PR won't reach this path again.
_route_pr_to_fix_worker "$pr_number" "$repo_slug" "$linked_issue" "review" "$_cr_pr_labels" || true
```

Alternatively, make the thread remediation a blocking check: if it succeeds (threads resolved), don't route to fix worker at all. This requires the scanner to return a success/fail signal.

## Verification

- Integration: PR with CHANGES_REQUESTED + fixable threads → thread remediation worker dispatched → log shows "review-thread remediation queued"
- Integration: if thread remediation succeeds and reviewer approves → next pulse cycle clears CHANGES_REQUESTED → PR proceeds to merge normally
- Regression: PR with coderabbit-nits-ok + CodeRabbit-only CHANGES_REQUESTED → code dismissal path still works (unaffected)
- Regression: PR with CHANGES_REQUESTED from human, no fixable threads → `_route_pr_to_fix_worker` still called as fallback

## Environment

- aidevops version: 3.31.49
- Latest version: 3.31.49
- AI Assistant: OpenCode
- OS: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- Shell: bash 5.2.21(1)-release
- Working repo: mesh-manager
- gh CLI: gh version 2.89.0 (2026-03-26)

## Additional Context

Related issues:
- #24512 (done) — Added `_pulse_merge_maybe_dispatch_review_thread_remediation` for merge-blocker path. This issue fixes the missing call for CHANGES_REQUESTED path.
- #25336 (consolidated) — Merge fallback losing GraphQL error context. Different trigger path.
- #25889 (done) — Thread-response worker cannot fix code. This issue is about calling remediation *at all* for CHANGES_REQUESTED, regardless of whether the worker can fix code.
- #25779 (closed) — fingerprint not passed to worker. Different issue about worker capability.
- #26533 (open) — `full-loop-helper.sh` missing `create-pr` alias causing unlabeled PRs. The PR that triggered this investigation (#1514) was missing `origin:worker` due to this bug.

```python
def build_tags(content: str, rows: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
```

title: bug: stale LLM lockdir cleanup blocked behind skip_llm guard in _pulse_maybe_run_llm_supervisor
body:
## Description

`_handle_stale_llm_lock` cleanup is gated behind `skip_llm` guard in `_pulse_maybe_run_llm_supervisor`. When `_should_run_llm_supervisor` returns false (backlog progressing / failure cooldown), stale LLM lockdir is never checked or cleaned. A crashed supervisor holds the lock indefinitely until `_should_run_llm_supervisor` eventually returns true again.

This causes hours-long deadlocks: no LLM supervisor runs because the stale lock blocks acquisition, but the lock is never cleaned because the cleanup code is only reached when the supervisor would have started anyway.

## Expected Behavior

Stale LLM lockdir should be detected and cleaned every pulse-wrapper cycle, regardless of whether `_should_run_llm_supervisor` wants to start a new session.

## Reproducer

**Symptom**: LLM supervisor does not run for hours after a crash. Log shows stale LLM lockdir cleared after 68+ min delay.

**Actual log evidence** (pulse-wrapper.log):

```
[pulse-wrapper] Starting pulse at 2026-07-04T17:39:02Z (trigger=stall)  ← session starts, then crashes
...
[pulse-wrapper] Stale LLM lockdir detected (owner PID 952643 is dead) — clearing (GH#20613)
[pulse-wrapper] Starting pulse at 2026-07-04T19:00:38Z (trigger=stall)  ← 81 min later
```

**Causal code**: `pulse-wrapper-cycle.sh:284-337`

```bash
_pulse_maybe_run_llm_supervisor() {
    local skip_llm=false
    if [[ "${PULSE_FORCE_LLM:-0}" != "1" ]] && ! _should_run_llm_supervisor; then
        skip_llm=true                          # ← early return path, lock NEVER checked
    fi

    if [[ "$skip_llm" == "false" ]]; then      # ← _handle_stale_llm_lock DOPIERO TU
        local llm_lockdir="${LOCKDIR}.llm"
        ...
        elif _handle_stale_llm_lock "$llm_lockdir"; then   # line 307
```

## Steps to Reproduce

1. LLM supervisor starts and crashes (SIGKILL/OOM/manual kill) before cleanup
2. `_should_run_llm_supervisor` returns false on subsequent cycles (backlog progressing OR failure cooldown)
3. Stale lock persists, blocking new supervisor sessions
4. Lock only cleared when `_should_run_llm_supervisor` eventually returns true (cooldown expires + backlog stalled)

## Workarounds Applied

- `PULSE_FORCE_LLM=1` bypasses `_should_run_llm_supervisor` and forces lock check+cleanup

## Fix

Move `_handle_stale_llm_lock` call outside the `skip_llm` guard — check and clean stale LLM lockdir every cycle before deciding whether to start a new session.

## Environment

- aidevops version: 3.31.51
- OS: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- Shell: bash 5.2.21(1)-release
- gh CLI: gh version 2.89.0 (2026-03-26)

## Additional Context

Related prior art: GH#20613 (added stale-lock detection), GH#20626 (review followup). The stale lock detection exists but is unreachable when the supervisor is in cooldown or backlog-progressing state.

title: Self-heal migrated Mac launchd routine failures
body:
## Problem

After migrating Macs, local aidevops launchd routines showed several recoverable-but-noisy failures:

- r905 memory pressure monitor logged Bash bad-substitution failures from Bash 4-only lowercase expansion when invoked by a stale or direct macOS /bin/bash path.
- shared split modules such as shared-todo-commit.sh could be missing transiently during hot deploy/agent replacement, causing scheduled helpers to fail instead of retrying.
- worker-watchdog could fail script directory resolution during deploy-time path replacement.
- stats-wrapper treated GitHub secondary-rate-limit / EX_TEMPFAIL dashboard update deferrals as launchd failures.
- stale com.aidevops.dashboard LaunchAgent kept respawning with EX_CONFIG even though r912 is disabled/unmanaged.

## Fix context

Patch branch: fix-launchd-routine-self-heal
Files:
- .agents/scripts/memory-pressure-monitor.sh
- .agents/scripts/shared-constants.sh
- .agents/scripts/worker-watchdog.sh
- .agents/scripts/stats-wrapper.sh
- .agents/scripts/setup/modules/migrations.sh
- setup.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-memory-pressure-monitor-service-exit.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-shared-constants-source-retry.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-worker-watchdog-find-workers.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-stats-wrapper-headless-export.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-legacy-dashboard-launchagent-cleanup.sh

## Verification

## Acceptance criteria
